cwe_name: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an OS Command ('OS Command Injection')

exact_cwe_mechanism.evidence: The code demonstrates direct string substitution of user-controlled href into a command template, then execution via shell without neutralization of shell metacharacters

connection.evidence: href flows from user-controlled URLs or editor input through string substitution directly to os.execv shell command execution

diff_causality.evidence: This line is the primary mechanism that substitutes user input into the command template, creating the injection vulnerability

security_control.evidence: No sanitization or shell escaping is applied to href before substitution
security_control.control_requirement_evidence: CWE-78 requires neutralization of shell metacharacters when constructing shell commands from external input
existing_controls_checked: encoder() function applied after substitution but purpose unclear
no shell escaping or parameterization observed
security_control.deficiency_evidence: href is directly substituted without any escaping, allowing shell metacharacters to modify command execution

concrete_impact.evidence: Arbitrary command execution is demonstrated through shell command injection mechanism

diff_counterfactual: If the candidate line were reverted, the substitution of user-controlled href into the shell command would not occur, preventing the command injection vulnerability.
supporting_evidence: href is user-controlled from URLs or editor input
path template contains %u placeholder for substitution
os.execv executes the substituted string via shell with -c flag
No escaping or sanitization applied to href before substitution
unresolved_facts: Exact security purpose of encoder() function
Whether browser configuration validation prevents malicious templates
review_comment: User-controlled href is directly substituted into a shell command template without escaping, allowing command injection. The patch introduces unsafe string substitution that enables shell metacharacters in href to modify command execution. Use shell escaping or parameterized execution to safely pass href as an argument rather than embedding it in the command string.
